name: GiveDirectly, Inc
mission:
GiveDirectly is a nonprofit that lets donors send money directly to the world’s poorest households. We believe people living in poverty deserve the dignity to choose for themselves how best to improve their lives — cash enables that choice.

Since 2009, we’ve delivered $700M+ in cash directly into the hands of over 1.5 million people living in poverty. We currently have operations in Bangladesh, DRC, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Mozambique, Morocco, Nigeria, Rwanda, Turkey, Uganda, USA, and Yemen.
theoryOfChange: GiveDirectly’s aims to reshape the social sector by establishing cash as a benchmark with the ultimate aim of ending poverty.

strengths_deep_dive: GiveDirectly operates a direct cash transfer model. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="3">$206,811,067 in total revenue</cite> while maintaining an <cite id="5">87.1% program expense ratio</cite>. This exceeds the sector standard benchmark of 75%. Furthermore, Charity Navigator rates GiveDirectly at <cite id="1">94/100 overall</cite>, giving it a perfect <cite id="1">100 score for financial accountability</cite>. These financial reserves provide <cite id="1">11.4 months of operating capital</cite>, ensuring strong operational resilience.
rich_narrative.summary: GiveDirectly provides direct cash assistance to people living in extreme poverty. Founded in 2009, <cite id="1">the organization has expanded operations</cite> across East Africa, including Kenya, Rwanda, Malawi, Liberia, and Uganda. In FY2024, GiveDirectly reported <cite id="3">a total revenue of $206,811,067</cite>, demonstrating significant financial scale. The organization maintains a high level of operational efficiency, directing <cite id="5">91.8% of expenses to program activities in FY2024</cite>, which beats the 75% industry standard benchmark. Direct cash transfers allow recipients to address their immediate priorities directly. The model is supported by extensive empirical research. While GiveDirectly holds an overall score of <cite id="1">94.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite> and a <cite id="14">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite>, it maintains a specific focus on unconditional cash relief rather than broad infrastructure development.
